slides.speaker_notes:
[0:00 - 0:25 | Slide 1: Introduction]
Judges, this is ReturnLens. For solo merchants, handling customer chat about order status, returns, and refunds is time-consuming and error-prone. ReturnLens handles routine inquiries while using video evidence to triage disputed claims. Models observe, deterministic code verifies, and the merchant always authorizes every consequential financial decision.

slides.speaker_notes:
[0:25 - 0:50 | Slide 2: The Problem]
A customer chats in: 'I ordered white headphones, but received black. Please refund me,' attaching an 18-second unboxing video. The seller currently checks four separate sources: chat, Shopify, courier tracking, and store policies. The seller needs verified facts before deciding whether to request more evidence, approve a return, or inspect the parcel.

slides.speaker_notes:
[0:50 - 1:30 | Slide 3: The Core Demonstration]
Here is our core demonstration. The Shopify order specifies white headphones, but the video shows black casing. ReturnLens flags this visible difference clearly. Notice our honest AI grounding: the package barcode remains unverified. Instead of guessing, ReturnLens prepares clear next steps. Option two drafts a polite clarification asking for the outer-box label, ready for one-click seller approval.

slides.speaker_notes:
[1:30 - 2:10 | Slide 4: Agent Behavior]
Our planned prototype executes real tools against a mock backend. The agent fetches order and tracking records, verifies the seven-day return window in code, and asks for one close-up photo if evidence is unclear. Refunds require seller approval, bounded by the remaining refundable amount (₹1,499) and our sample store cap of ₹3,000. Every tool call and outcome is logged.

slides.speaker_notes:
[2:10 - 2:35 | Slide 5: Three Scenarios]
Our prototype handles three distinct branches: In Case A, verified delivery dates produce a draft return label. In Case B, color discrepancies trigger a single clarification request. In Case C, unclear evidence activates refund guardrails and escalates directly to the merchant. All actions remain transparent and audit-logged.

[2:35 - 3:00 | Slide 6: Execution Roadmap & Closing]
In our 24-hour sprint, four teammates build in parallel against a shared schema: tool execution, vision extraction, seller UI, and integration testing. Build first includes real tool calls on mock data and safety guardrails, saving live production APIs for later. ReturnLens: one clear evidence pack. The seller makes the call.

qa_defense.question: How does the vision model handle blurry or low-quality video?
qa_defense.answer: Fail-closed architecture: The model only asserts what is clear. If unboxing footage is too dark or blurry (Case C), ReturnLens flags low confidence and requests a single close-up photo of the product or outer label, appending it to the existing case file without auto-rejecting. If still unclear after one request, the case escalates directly to the seller.

qa_defense.question: Why not automate refunds entirely to save time for solo sellers?
qa_defense.answer: Automating financial transactions from customer-submitted video is a severe fraud vector (friendly fraud and refund abuse). ReturnLens adheres to strict authority boundaries: models observe and code verifies, but the seller always authorizes returns, shipping labels, and refunds.

qa_defense.question: How will a 4-person team deliver this prototype in 24 hours?
qa_defense.answer: Disciplined scoping: The team focuses on Sprint Core deliverables—real tool calls against mock fixtures, keyframe extraction, deterministic policy rules with refund caps, and a side-by-side seller console covering Cases A, B, and C. Live production store and courier integrations are deferred.

qa_defense.question: How is ReturnLens different from general CS chat agents like Zendesk or Intercom?
qa_defense.answer: General CS bots handle text chat and FAQ resolution. ReturnLens is a multimodal evidence triage assistant specifically designed for physical merchandise claims. It links physical unboxing video keyframes with catalog specifications and store policies to build a structured decision dossier for the merchant.

qa_defense.question: How do you prevent hallucinations in the claim assessment?
qa_defense.answer: Separation of concerns: The vision model only describes physical observations (e.g., color=Black). Deterministic code compares strings (Black != White) and checks dates against policy (0 <= current_date - delivery_date <= 7 days). The system never speculates on intent or fraud, presenting raw facts for merchant review.
